name: NGC 4900, SN 1999br field (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 4900, a barred spiral galaxy and host of SN 1999br, seen by Hubble.
label: sn1999br-hubble
story: In 1999 the supernova SN 1999br flared in NGC 4900, one of a small group of unusually faint, low-energy Type II explosions. Hubble came back to study the stars around the site, to estimate how massive the star that exploded was.

claims.text: SN 1999br is a Type II supernova in NGC 4900
NGC 4900 is classified SB(rs)c, a barred spiral
SN 1999br belongs to a small group of low-luminosity, low-energy Type II supernovae
Hubble program 17070 images Type II supernova sites to resolve the surrounding stars and estimate progenitor initial masses
